title: Build an Interpreter in Rust
summary: Build a lexer, Pratt parser, lexical closures and diagnostics, then compile a language to bytecode and run it on your own VM.
description: Construct a small language in fourteen cumulative, standalone exercises: tokenization with source positions, a peekable token stream, Pratt expression parsing, checked evaluation, a calculator review, shared environments, statements, control flow, functions and mutable closures, readable diagnostics, a persistent-session review, bytecode compilation, a stack virtual machine and jump backpatching. Every starter includes the previous working layers; hidden tests vary programs and error cases. The bytecode engine deliberately supports a smaller, flat-scope subset of the tree interpreter.
